Program Analysis

Symbolic Execution

02 June 2026 · Nine minutes

Symbolic execution is a means of analyzing a program to determine what inputs cause each part of it to execute. Instead of running the code on real values, an interpreter walks it while holding every input as a symbol.

It arrives at expressions written in terms of those symbols, and at constraints for the outcome of each conditional branch. Where concrete execution answers what a program does with 5, symbolic execution answers what it would take to reach a place at all.

A worked example

int f() {
  y = read();
  z = y * 2;
  if (z == 12) fail();
  else printf("OK");
}

During symbolic execution the program reads a symbol, λ, and the branch condition becomes the constraint λ * 2 == 12. Execution forks, and a solver later returns 6 to reach fail().

Limitations

  • Merge states that differ only in irrelevant ways, and accept weaker constraints.
  • Bound loop iterations, and accept incompleteness past the bound.
  • Prioritize paths heuristically, and accept that the interesting one may be starved.
Program testing can be used to show the presence of bugs, but never to show their absence.
